nodes.text: APPENDIX TO THE BOOKS OF KINGS.
On the unity of faith, and on charity, which is the fullness of the law.

1. Why one man? Not only is that one man called one, but all who are fit are called one. All who have the one wisdom confess the one Christ Jesus; they are filled with the one Spirit of God; hence the Apostle says: All indeed run, but one receives the prize (1 Cor. 9:24).

2. Each of the foolish is not one but many, because according to Scripture the fool changes like the moon. The moon, though it is seen to be one in substance, is always other than itself and varied through the change of days; so are sinners, who are always changing in knowledge and desire various things.

3. God, however, is called one not by number, but because he never becomes other than himself. Therefore he never changes, as it is written: But you are the same, and your years will not fail (Ps. 101:28).

4. From Mount Ephraim. That is, not from the valleys, nor from the plains, not from the hills. From Mount Ephraim, which is interpreted 'fruitfulness'; that is, then, from the fruit-bearing mountain. The Lord says: The Lord of the mountains, not of the valleys.

5. Elkanah is interpreted 'possession of God'. That man had two wives: the first, the nobler, Hannah, was barren, as Abraham's first wife, the nobler Sarah, was barren; the second, the Egyptian Hagar, was less noble. And Abraham became a father by the less noble one, yet so that afterwards he became a father by the noble wife.

6. So Elkanah, who is 'possession of God', first becomes a father by the second wife, because God had closed the womb of Hannah, as earlier the womb of Sarah. After Peninnah had given birth, God opened Hannah's womb. Peninnah is interpreted 'conversion'; Hannah is interpreted 'grace'.

7. Whoever wishes to become a possession of God, let him take these two wives, and join to himself first the one who is nobler, grace; for she is joined first, through faith, as the Apostle says: For by the grace of God you have been saved through faith (Eph. 2:8). Second he is joined to Peninnah, that is, to conversion, because after the grace of belief comes the amendment of conduct.

8. Peninnah bears sons to us first, because we bring forth our first fruits. And unless we turn away from evil, we will not be able to become fathers by Hannah. Peninnah has sons, but ones who do not stand in attendance; yet they are not empty, for they eat of the divine sacrifices.

9. So everyone who turns away from sin begets works of righteousness out of conversion. And afterwards Hannah, roused by good zeal, pours out prayer to the Lord, that she herself may bear sons who stand before God, that is, sons of grace, who are free for God. In the Gospel the pattern of this story is shown.

10. Namely, Martha is busy about much serving: she fulfils the works of conduct, and through these, as it were, begets sons of conduct. And Mary, sitting at the feet of the Lord's word, is said to have chosen the best part, and is understood, as it were, to beget twin graces.

11. So Hannah bears a son, Samuel, who stands before God, of whom it is said: Moses and Aaron among his priests, and Samuel among those who call upon his name (Ps. 98:6); [the name] is interpreted 'There God himself [is]'. For where the spirit of grace is, there God is said to be, as Paul says: And falling on his face he worshipped God, saying: Truly God is among you.

12. Unless the works of conversion come first, we cannot beget the gifts of the Spirit in Shiloh. Shiloh is the name of the place in which sacrifices were offered before the temple was built in Jerusalem, and the cleansing of sins took place. Shiloh is interpreted 'uprooting', or 'unshoeing', that is, the loosing of the shoe. The place in which sins are cleansed is called 'uprooting', where the heart of stone is uprooted; and 'unshoeing', because all of us are shod until we come to the holy place; but when we arrive at it, we are ordered to take off our shoes.

13. As is said to Moses: Loose the strap of your shoe, for the place on which you stand is holy ground (Exod. 3:5), so that he might cast off the marks of mortality, which are signified by shoes of hide. Hence the Saviour says: Nor shoes on your feet, since they were to walk that way. He says: I am the way, and the truth, and the life. For no one walks the way of life with a mark of mortality.
14. Shiloh, where Eli is, a man less praiseworthy; for on account of sin he fell backwards and died. If anyone turns back from faith and truth, he must fall and die at once.

15. Eli is interpreted 'stranger'; a stranger indeed to God is he who does not keep discipline, and does not take thought for his son, does not rebuke or correct [him], who indulges vices. Eli's son Hophni is interpreted 'height of conversion', because he becomes far from cleansing, which turns [one] to the Lord.

16. We know two Phinehases in Scripture: the righteous one, son of Aaron, and the unrighteous one, son of Eli. Phinehas signifies 'stopping of the mouth' and 'sparing the mouth'. Both are among priests today: he who spares his mouth, and from whom, as a priest, no evil word proceeds, is compared to Phinehas son of Aaron. Compared to the son of Eli are those priests who have their mouth stopped, whether through ignorance or vice, or through consciousness of sins.

17. Until she weaned him from milk. Samuel is weaned from the rational milk of Hannah, because he who is offered to God could not be offered before he was weaned from milk, as long as he is a child in understanding; Paul says: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food.

18. Everyone who first turns from heresy to the faith is nourished with milk: the word of righteousness is foreign [to him], and he has no faculties for discerning good and evil. A little child cannot go up to the temple of God, nor be present at the ministries of the priests; but neither does his mother go up, though she could go up; for grace is his mother, who keeps him and nourishes him.

19. And Hannah prayed, and said: She is not found to pray except through two sayings only, and she says: I have rejoiced in your salvation. And the other is: For there is no God besides you. But the Apostle says: Pray without ceasing (1 Thess. 5:17).

20. He who is engaged in the divine office: all his deeds and words we count as prayer, because the righteous man does without ceasing what is righteous. For this reason the righteous man will pray without ceasing. And in the Psalms he says: The lifting up of my hands [is] an evening sacrifice (Ps. 140).

21. He lifts up his hands: his deeds. Otherwise: when Moses lifted up his hand, Israel prevailed, but when he let it down, Amalek prevailed, because as long as the servant lifts up his deeds to the Lord, the people of God prevails; but when he lets down his deeds, Amalek, the enemy of God, prevails.

22. Hannah says: My heart has exulted. Of necessity she added: in the Lord. As Paul said: Rejoice in the Lord (Phil. 4:4). For one can rejoice in carnal things. When men praise me, I do not rejoice in the Lord; if I rejoice, may I be pricked.

23. Because of the word of the Lord, the horns of the righteous. That is, saying: In you we will toss our enemies with the horn (Ps. 43:6). In the Greek, a joyful testimony. Therefore we butt with the horn, or toss with the horn. The horns of the righteous, because they are conferred on the righteous from the tips of the cross of Christ.

24. With these we will destroy the hostile powers from our soul. Then a vineyard is planted in us. My mouth is enlarged, that is, through meditation on the word of God we may come to the lifting up of the heart, as the Apostle too says: Our mouth is opened wide to you, O Corinthians (2 Cor. 6:11). For from the height of the heart wisdom is supplied to the mouth.

25. Because I have rejoiced in your salvation, that is, if I have rejoiced in the salvation of the Lord, then my mouth is enlarged. There is none holy as God. She uses a distinction: she did not say 'except the Lord', but 'there is none as the Lord'. There is no God besides you, that is, none of those things which exist by nature. You who alone are; to whom what you are was given by no one. For a shadow too is nothing in comparison with a body, and smoke is nothing in comparison with fire.

26. Do not multiply speaking lofty things. As Solomon says: Do not seek things higher than you (Ecclus. 3:22). Concerning the things commanded you, understand these: do not multiply speaking, except of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, so that what we speak may become more fully manifest. After these three, speak nothing.

27. Let no idle talk go out of your mouth, as the Apostle says: Who will deliver me from the body of this death (Rom. 7:24)? Otherwise: An angel of Satan, to buffet me (2 Cor. 12:7). That is, lest I speak great things of myself. Let no boasting go out of your mouth. Do not incline my heart to words of malice, to make excuses in sins (Ps. 140:4).

28. And Solomon says: The sluggard seeks excuses, and says: There is a lion outside. He also says: The devil will mock me, as the woman seduced me (Prov. 18:1; 22:13). The just man is first the accuser of himself; the unjust man is not the accuser of himself, but of others. As long as someone sins, he is neither just nor an accuser of himself. For he who does [the deed] does not accuse [it].

29. The bow of the mighty is weakened. If you are clothed with the arms of God, with the shield of faith, and the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the spirit, the bow of the mighty will be strengthened by such defences. And the weak are girded with strength, as it is [written]: The foolish things of the world God has chosen, to confound the strong (1 Cor. 1:27).

30. The weak people is the Gentile people, which, a stranger to the Testament of God, has gained strength, as the Prophet says: The Lord is my strength and my praise (Ps. 117:14); that is, strength is Christ himself. Until the barren one, our mother, is the Church. And she has borne seven, that is, the sevenfold number.

31. And my flesh, having very many fruits of the flesh: fornication, uncleanness, unchastity, idolatry, sorceries, quarrels, rivalries, provocations, dissensions. Barren, that is, the soul, which at one time did not bring forth the fruits of justice, nor was filled through faith in Christ with the spirit of wisdom, and of understanding, and of counsel, and of fortitude, and of knowledge, and of piety, and of the fear of God.

32. God kills, and makes alive. He kills me when I was dead to sin, and then he makes me alive when he makes me live to God. The true David, keeping his father's sheep, seized the lion and killed it. The title of the psalm is: For David himself, when his son was persecuting him.

33. We read that this happened in the books of Kings: that he, not loved unjustly but humbled piously, received discipline from the Lord, and endured a remedy, not a requital for iniquity. That David [was] [...], but another David, strong of hand, [is] the Lord Jesus Christ.

34. For those past deeds were figures of things to come. Let us recognise how Christ too was persecuted by his son. Christ had sons, of whom he said: The sons of the bridegroom do not fast as long as the bridegroom is with them. Among these was the persecutor Judas.
On the marriage of a deceased man's kinsman or brother.

35. By the law the marriage of a dead man's wife was conferred on his kinsman or brother, so that he might raise up seed for his brother or kinsman. Hence it is that Ruth, though herself a foreigner, yet because she had had a husband from the Jews, who had left behind a surviving kinsman, was seen and loved by Boaz as she gathered the sheaves of his harvest, with which to feed her mother-in-law.

36. He did not take her as wife until the one to whom she was owed as wife by the law had first loosed his shoe. The story is simple, but the mysteries deep; for one thing was being done, another was being figured. For it designated the Christ to come from the Jews, who would raise up the seed of his kinsman, that is, of the dead people, with the seed of heavenly teaching.

37. To whom did the spiritual prescriptions of the law assign the nuptial shoe for being joined to the Church? Moses was not the bridegroom. For to him it is said: Loose your shoes, lest from the likeness of the name he be believed the bridegroom of the Church. There was no other bridegroom but Christ alone, of whom John said: He who has the bride is the bridegroom (John 3:29).

38. So the shoe of the one is loosed; that of the other cannot be loosed, as John says: I am not worthy to loose the strap, and the rest. Christ alone, then, is the bridegroom: for whom that bride, coming from the Gentiles, once destitute and hungry, but now rich with Christ's harvest and married, binds in the inner lap of her mind the sheaves of the fruitful crop, the remnants of the word, so that she may feed with new nourishment that widow exhausted by the death of her son, the destitute mother of a dead people, not leaving her forsaken, and seeking new ones.

39. Christ alone, then, is the bridegroom, who does not begrudge even the synagogue the sheaves of his harvest. Would that she did not shut herself out! She had [those] whom she might have gathered by herself; because her people is dead, as though her native son had died, she was gathering through the Church sheaves on which to live, which they carried coming in rejoicing, as it is written: But coming they shall come, and the rest.

40. Elkanah, the father of the venerable Samuel, who was the possession of God; for Elkanah is translated 'into the possession of God'; he is called a man for the virtue of his mind, and not only a man, but he is also called one man. For he was not carried about wandering in different directions, as if changeable and unstable, but persisting firm and unshaken, he was one man.

41. And for that reason he dwelt on the fruitful mount Ephraim, that is, in the lofty contemplation of the virtues, so that the height of his mind might not be cast down, nor its unity split, by any thoughts of vices lying beneath and barking around [it].

42. David, fleeing with his companions from the face of Saul, figured Christ, who with the apostles was hidden from the prince of the world, except only from the priests, so as to show that the priestly food would pass over to the use of the prophet; whether because we all ought to imitate the priestly life, or because all the sons of the Church are priests, offering themselves to God as spiritual sacrifices.

43. So David entered the priest's house, and the priest, though the danger of death was set before him, did not refuse the guest; so that, morally, we may willingly take others' dangers upon ourselves for the sake of hospitality, or, mystically, that priests may not shut Christ out of the hospitality of their mind even when death and ruin are foreseen.

44. Where Christ, taking the spoils of spiritual wickedness, stripped that Goliath of his spoils and arms, there David asked for loaves. But he received one, because food is prepared for the faithful not from the five books of Moses but from the body of Christ.

45. Doeg, however, keeper of the camels, an unfruitful flock, fulfils the type of Judas the betrayer. But in the house of Ahimelech Abiathar alone, chief of the priests, escaped unharmed from the persecutor Saul, because no one can harm Christ, the chief of priests.

46. What then? Because David, who did not return evil to one who repaid him evil, when Saul and Jonathan fell in battle, cursed the mountains of Gilboa, saying: Mountains of Gilboa, let neither dew nor rain come upon you, nor let there be fields of firstfruits, because there the shield of Saul was cast away, as though he had not been anointed with oil. What then? When Saul died, did the mountains sin, so that neither dew nor rain should fall on them? But because Gilboa is interpreted 'a running down', and through Saul, anointed and dead, the death of the Mediator is expressed, not undeservedly are the proud hearts of the Jews signified by the mountains of Gilboa: which, while they flow down into the desires of this world, have involved themselves in the death of Christ, that is, of the Anointed.

47. And because the anointed king dies bodily upon them, they themselves are dried up from all dew of grace, and of them it is well said that they cannot be fields of firstfruits. For the proud minds of the Hebrews do not bear the first fruits, because at the coming of the Redeemer, remaining for the most part in unbelief, they would not follow the beginnings of the faith.

48. For holy Church, made fruitful in the firstfruits by the multitude of the Gentiles, scarcely at the end of the world receives the Jews whom she finds; gathering the last, she sets them as the remnants of the crops; of whom Isaiah [says]: If the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved (Isa. 10:22).

49. Finally, the mountains of Gilboa can be cursed from the prophet's mouth for this reason: that while no fruit springs up as the earth dries out, the owners may nevertheless be struck with the loss of barrenness, so that they themselves should receive the sentence of the curse, because they had deserved, as their iniquity demanded, to undergo the death of the king among them.

50. Thus very often a thing is a virtue in the history, a fault in the signification. Just as sometimes a deed done is a cause of damnation in the act, but in the writing a prophecy of virtue. This we show more quickly to be true if we bring the deed of David into the open, proving both points by one testimony.

51. Who, hearing it, not only among the faithful but even among the unbelievers themselves, does not detest that David, walking on the roof, coveted Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah? Yet when he returned from battle, he urged him to go home and wash his feet. He at once replied, saying: The ark of God is under skins, and shall I rest in my house?

52. David received him at his own table, and handed him letters by which he was to die. But whose type does David walking on the roof bear, if not his of whom it is written: He has set his tabernacle in the sun (Ps. 18:6)? And what is it to take Bathsheba, if not to join to himself by spiritual understanding the law of the letter that was joined to the carnal people?

53. For Bathsheba is called 'the seventh well', because indeed through the knowledge of the law, by the infusion of spiritual grace, perfect wisdom is ministered to us. And whom does Uriah signify, if not the Jewish people? whose name is said to be interpreted 'my light of God'. But the Jewish people, because it is lifted up by the knowledge of the law it received, glories as it were in the light of God.

54. But David took the wife from this Uriah and joined her to himself, because, namely, the strong of hand, who is called David, appearing as Redeemer in the flesh, when he made known that the law spoke of him spiritually, by this showed her, as held according to the letter, to be estranged from the Jewish people, and joined her to himself, who declared that he was proclaimed through her.

55. Yet David urges Uriah to go to his house and wash his feet, because the incarnate Lord, coming to the Jewish people, commanded that it return to its conscience and wipe away the filth of its works, so that it might understand the commands of the law spiritually, and, finding after such harshness of precepts the font of baptism, might run back to the water after its toil.

56. But Uriah, who remembered that the ark of God was under skins, replied that he could not enter his house. As if the Jewish people were to say: I see the commands of God in carnal sacrifices, and I do not seek to return to conscience through spiritual understanding. For he as it were says that the ark is under skins who understands the precepts of God only as for performing the service of carnal sacrifice.

57. Yet David calls him even when he is unwilling to return to his house. Because although the Jewish people scorns to turn back to conscience, yet the Redeemer, coming, preaches the spiritual commands, saying: If you believed Moses, you would perhaps believe me also; for he wrote of me (John 5:46).

58. So the Jewish people holds the law, since it speaks of the divinity of him in whom that same people disdains to believe. Hence also Uriah is sent with letters to Joab, by which he was to be killed, because that same Jewish people carries the law by whose conviction it dies. For while, retaining the commands of the law, it strives to fulfil them, it itself indeed bears the judgement by which it is condemned.

59. For Gaza, and Ashkelon, and Ekron will undergo different punishments. Gaza is interpreted 'its strength'. So all who applaud themselves in strength of body and worldly power, and say with the devil: I will do mighty deeds, will be plundered in the day of the Lord's wrath, and brought to nothing.

60. Ashkelon indeed, which is interpreted 'weights', or 'fire of the murderer', when the day of wrath comes, will feel the measure of its crime, and be pressed down by the same weight with which it worked. And because it burned to shed blood, and caused many souls to stumble, and in it was fulfilled: The man of blood and deceit the Lord abhors, it will not be plundered, like Gaza, but, reduced to a wilderness, will be burned up by the fires of Gehenna down to dust.

61. Also Ashdod, which in Hebrew is called [...], and in our language means 'fire of generation', will bear witness in clear light. For it burned with lust, and was destroyed by the burning of generation; and because all are adulterers, their hearts like an oven, they have also been wounded by burning arrows. Not in darkness, not in a hidden judgement, but at noon, that is, when the saints receive full brightness, they will be cast into darkness, and will not have the fellowship of the saints on the day of judgement.

62. And Ekron too, which is interpreted 'barrenness' or 'uprooting', because it had no fruit, and by the perversity of its teaching uprooted very many, will itself be uprooted. Understand all these varieties in the vices and sins of souls. And the fire will test what sort each one's work is. For this reason the weak often pass judgement on many things that are said by the strong, because they do not know that, when that ark of the Covenant tilted with the oxen kicking, the Levite, believing it was about to fall, wished to set it upright, and at once received the sentence of condemnation.

63. For what is the mind of the just man, if not the ark of the Covenant? It tilts as it is carried by kicking oxen, because sometimes even one who rules well, while he is subject [to them], stirred by the turmoil of the peoples, is moved out of love alone to condescend by way of dispensation. But in what is done by dispensation, this very tilting is thought by the unskilled to be a fall of strength. Hence also some subordinates put out the hand of reproof against it, but at once the very merits of their life fail.

64. He is rightly called Uzzah, which is interpreted 'strong one of the Lord'. Since all presumptuous people, unless with bold mind they believed themselves strong in the Lord, would never judge the deeds or words of better men as weak.

65. I will give you kings in my fury. If therefore, when God is angry, we receive rulers according to our merits, we read in their conduct what we should weigh by our own estimation, although for the most part the elect are subject to the reprobate. Hence David too endured Saul, because he was then worthy to be oppressed by such harshness of a superior. So therefore the persons of rulers are allotted according to the merits of subjects, so that often those who seem good are changed as soon as they have taken up rule, as Scripture says: Who changed his heart with his rank.

66. Hence it is written: Behold, when you were little in your own eyes, I made you head among the tribes of Israel. So the acts of rulers are disposed according to the qualities of subjects, so that often, because of the wickedness of the flock, the life even of a truly good shepherd goes astray. For that David, praised by God's own testimony, that prophet aware of heavenly things, sinned by numbering the people. And yet, when David sinned, the people received the punishment.

67. Why this? Clearly because the order of rulers is disposed through the merit of the peoples. But the just judge punished the fault of the sinner by chastising those on whose account he sinned. Yet because, growing proud by his own will, he was not free of the fault, he too received the punishment of the fault. For the raging wrath that struck the people bodily also laid low the ruler of the people with inward grief of heart.

68. And the cows went straight along the road that leads to Beth-shemesh, going on and lowing, and they turned aside neither to the right nor to the left. What then do the cows signify, if not all the faithful in the Church? Who, while they consider the precepts of the sacred word, carry as it were the ark of the Lord placed upon them.

69. Of whom this too is to be noted beforehand, that they are recorded to have had calves, because there are many who, set inwardly on the way of God, are bound outwardly by carnal affections, but do not turn aside from the right road, since they carry the ark of the Lord. For behold, Beth-shemesh means 'house of the sun'. And the Prophet says: But for you who fear the name of the Lord the sun of righteousness will rise (Mal. 4:2). If therefore we are making for the dwelling of the eternal sun, it is surely fitting that we do not turn aside from God's road for carnal affections.

70. For it must be weighed with all our strength that the cows yoked to God's cart go on and groan; they give lowings from deep within, and yet do not turn their steps from the road. So indeed the preachers of God's word, so the teachers, so all the faithful within holy Church ought to be, that they suffer with their neighbours through charity, and yet do not stray from the way of God through compassion.

71. Snow, then, can be understood now as the brightness of innocence and grace, now as the winter and cold of charity. And as to what we read in the books of Kings, that a certain Benaiah, one of the mighty men of Israel, went down into a cistern and struck a lion in time of snow, I think snow is placed in those passages without distinction, because both the grace of Christ, which shone out in this world, and the cold of the love of God, in which men grew cold, could be signified by sacred Scripture under the name of snow.

72. Benaiah we understand figuratively as the Saviour, because according to the force of his name he is the Lord the builder; of whom the prophet had foretold, since he said that the Church was to be built by him: The Lord building Jerusalem. And again: He has built Zion; which word Scripture used in its proper sense in the making of Eve, who bore the type of the Church, saying: And the Lord God built the rib, which he had taken from Adam, into a woman. And Paul, seeing her being built, says: You are God's building.

73. Why is Samuel called three times? Because he was prophet, priest and leader. David first reigned 40 years from the tribe of Judah. Rehoboam ... years, Abijah ..., Asa the just ..., Joram ..., Ahaziah ..., Athaliah ..., Joash ..., Amaziah ..., Azariah ..., Jotham ..., Ahaz ..., Hezekiah ..., Manasseh ..., Amon ..., Josiah ..., Joash ..., Eliakim ..., Jehoiachin ..., Hezekiah ..., Astraph ...: 14, 3 years, 41, 7 years, 50 years, 4 years, 11 years, 6 years, 14 years, 16 years, 29 years, 55 years.
RUBRIC.
Here begin the chapters on the book of Ezra. On the seventy years of the captivity, etc.
